profile.name: Ali Bayramli
profile.title: Senior Software Engineer
profile.headline: I build web applications and Backstage developer platforms.
profile.summary: Senior Software Engineer with 8+ years building web applications, including trading interfaces built with Angular and internal developer platforms built on Backstage. I design reusable components and automate provisioning, configuration, and access management.
profile.availability: Open to remote software engineering roles and projects
profile.contactHeadline: Open to remote software engineering roles and projects.

bullets: Design Backstage templates with shared provisioning, configuration, and access automation, reducing duplication and saving ~3,000 engineering hours monthly.
Lead development of golden paths, scorecards, and service catalog workflows for a Backstage internal developer platform (IDP) in an organization of 1,000+ developers.
Build Backstage plugins that use the Azure AI SDK to validate service catalog metadata.
Mentor new team members on the codebase and development tools.

proofMetric.label: Engineering hours saved/month
proofMetric.note: XM.com - automated provisioning, configuration, and access management.

bullets: Contributed to the Angular architecture and built reusable UI components for Trading.com’s launch in Europe and Australia.
Defined Angular component APIs that kept trading rules in each application, allowing teams to reuse components across products.
Helped migrate 15+ wealth management applications from desktop to web, keeping existing backend APIs to support an incremental rollout.
Implemented responsive data grids and real-time UI updates with Angular and AG Grid.
Helped move email generation and styling to an internal web platform, reducing annual third-party tooling costs by ~$100K.
Built a gamified employee engagement dashboard with Vue.js and Node.js.

projects.title: Template Pulse
projects.description: Built a Backstage plugin with React.js and Node.js to track software template adoption, success rates, and execution times, with searchable run history and permission-based access.
caseStudy: Shows which software templates developers use, how often runs succeed, and how long they take.
Helps teams investigate problems with filters, searchable run history, and links to the original tasks.
Lets developers review their own activity and authorized team members see template usage across the organization.
